packet.headline_seed: Alan Jones trial live updates: former radio broadcaster in Sydney court for day two of indecent assault case – latest news
packet.description_seed: Former 2UE and 2GB radio broadcaster is facing 22 charges. Jones, 85, has pleaded not guilty Warning: This live blog may contain graphic content when discussing evidence in the trial Jones allegedly gifted cash and car to teenager he kissed after commenting on sprinter’s penis, trial hears The trial is expected to resume at 10am with complainant J continuing his evidence. I’m in court now with Amanda Meade to follow all the developments on day two. If you want a summary of what happened yesterday, you can read Ben Doherty’s analysis below: The booming voice, the vast radio audience, the bully pulpit of an eponymous TV show, the great and the good on speed-dial, a staffer in the prime ministerial office dubbed the ‘minister for Alan Jones’: these were not ancillaries peripheral to the Jones empire, they were central to it. Even walking into court on Monday, at the centre of a glacially moving press pack, it was all about Alan. Continue reading...

Alan Jones has arrived in the courtroom. The proceedings are expected to kick off again in a moment.

On day one of the trial, the court heard several of the nine alleged indecent assaults against complainant J.

In case you missed our live coverage yesterday, below is a wrap of what was alleged in the first day of J’s evidence in chief.

Once J’s evidence in chief on each of the nine allegations is complete, he will be cross-examined by Alan Jones’s legal team.

Alan Jones first met complainant J when he was 14 years old and a star school athlete and “praised” him about his sports ability.

J alleged that Jones made a weekly deposit of $400 a week into his bank account and told him he didn’t have to tell anyone because it was a gift.

J, who was a teenager at the time, alleged that he was asked to drive Jones to a function in Canberra, and while the pair were alone in the hotel room Jones allegedly kissed him in a “smothering” way.

J alleged that after the Canberra incident Jones told him he had “been a really good boy” and increased his weekly stipend.

J told the court he didn’t tell his coach about an alleged incident because he “felt I’d lose everything” and said that he had “come from a small family” and “was getting everything handed” to him and it was a “wonderful life”.

J alleged that one of the indecent assault incidents occurred while he was driving Jones to his Fitzroy Falls farm and Jones grabbed his penis over his pants and then under his underpants.

The trial is expected to resume at 10am with complainant J continuing his evidence. I’m in court now with Amanda Meade to follow all the developments on day two.
